newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev closes flat at 1,595-1,600 to dollar.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev closes flat at 1,595-1,600 to dollar.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev closed at 1,595-1,600 per dollar, in a narrower spread from the morning's 1,590-1,610, after a calm interbank trade, dealers said.

"Relatively small foreign currency volumes were changing hands today. The bid/ask spread for the dollar tightened to five to 10 levs from 20-30 in past several days due to the stable balance between demand and supply," one dealer said.
As in the past days dollar sellers were mostly final clients, while the central bank was seen as the main buyer.
"If the central bank has not bought dollars for several days in a row, the dollar might have fallen to around 1,200 due to higher foreign currency supply from clients," another dealer said.

Banks' clients have intensified dollar sales since Thursday due to the recent lev stability between 1,570-1,600, which was supported by a financial accord between the interim government and the International Monetary Fund reached on Monday.
But the lev fell to 1,540-1,550 at exchange shops from 1,480-1,500 on Tuesday due to increased dollar demand from exchange offices for covering contracted payments to banks, traders said.

Exchange offices opted for contracting foreign currency sales to banks on Monday and Tuesday because lev/dollar exchange rates stood at 1,580-1,600 on the interbank market against 1,480-1,520 at exchange shops. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
